title: Elodie and the Spire
premise: Edmund Fairweather, royal food-taster and secret charm-seller in a city where magic is punishable by the Spire's silence, takes in a feral child who speaks the First Tongue and slowly realizes she is a soul that was sold to the court beneath the mountain — and that he himself sold it there three years ago to buy his immunity. To save her, Edmund must descend into the court of the mountain's dead magistrates, barter with the thing wearing his own remembered face, and choose between his accumulated protection and her stolen life. He gives up every charm, every year of immunity, and his own name in the ledger, returning the child whole but erasing himself from the city's memory; the final chapter belongs to Elodie, grown and remembering for both of them.
about_author: Oscar Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in systems older than their governments, and lives quietly near a mountain he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet him mid-routine: tasting the magistrate's soup, counting his charms, keeping his head down in a city that burned its mages. A child appears at his door speaking a language no kingdom has used, and when she touches his ledger, the entries rearrange into words he wrote three years ago — including one sale he doesn't remember making. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Immunity Cost
chapters.summary: Alternating Edmund and Elodie POV. Edmund investigates the ledger while hiding the girl from Spire wardens; Elodie's chapters are fragments of memory from inside the court beneath the mountain. He learns the truth: he sold a soul — hers — to gain his immunity, and the payment comes due on the winter solstice. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve as he decides to go down and take her back.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with Elodie along in secret. They descend through the abandoned mine-roads into the court of dead magistrates, where justice is administered by a thing that wears the faces of everyone who ever bargained with it. Edmund faces his own face across the bench and tries to argue the contract void; the court offers him a loophole that would keep his immunity if he lets Elodie stay. Climax: he tears up his own page instead. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Remembering for Two
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The city wakes with no record of Edmund Fairweather — not the taster, not the charm-seller, not the man who fed her. She alone carries him, in the First Tongue, which cannot be erased because it predates all ledgers. She takes up his small trade in charms, keeps his ledger open under a new name, and begins teaching other hidden children the old words. Final beat: grief braided with hope — memory as an act of justice outside any law.
